query: How can we improve incident resolution efficiency?

per_column.name: resolution_time_hours
per_column.rationale: Resolution time is a direct operationalization of resolution efficiency itself (the focus), not a treatment or confounder. It is essentially the outcome measure restated.

per_column.name: priority_level
per_column.rationale: Priority is set by triage and influences both how incidents are handled (e.g. reassignment/assignment decisions) and resolution efficiency. It is a plausible common cause not named in the query. It could also be argued to be a partially intervenable lever, but functions primarily as a confounder here.

per_column.name: is_reassigned
per_column.rationale: Reassignment is an actionable, settable operational lever: management can decide whether/how often to reassign tickets, making it a genuine intervenable treatment on resolution efficiency.

per_column.name: resolution_efficiency_tier
per_column.rationale: A bucketed (Slow/Medium/Fast) version of resolution efficiency; it is a restatement/binning of the outcome, not a treatment or confounder.

judge.rationale: The set contains a genuine intervenable treatment (is_reassigned), satisfying claim (a): reassignment is an operational decision an actor can set. However, the confounding structure (claim b) is weak. Two of the four added columns (resolution_time_hours, resolution_efficiency_tier) merely restate/bin the outcome and contribute nothing to confounder adjustment. Only priority_level serves as a plausible common cause of both reassignment and resolution efficiency, and it is a single, fairly obvious confounder. There is no adjustment for other common causes such as assignment_group workload/skill, category complexity, or caller/agent factors — precisely the kind of not-named-in-query confounders that would demonstrate the capability. Thus the counterfactual effect of reassignment cannot be cleanly read off; the interventional setup is only partially realized.
